subject.title: Stability, installer auth, runtime compatibility, and context-management improvements

question: Should #86567 remain open as the coordination umbrella, or should maintainers split the remaining work into narrow canonical issues and close the umbrella after links are established?
rationale: The remaining behavior crosses credential persistence, OAuth propagation, installer/update atomicity, provider fallback visibility, and session/context-management semantics that require explicit maintainer ownership and security posture.

options.title: Split Into Canonicals
options.body: Keep this issue open only long enough to create or confirm focused canonical issues for each remaining auth, installer, runtime, and session-state surface, then close the umbrella once every acceptance criterion is owned.

options.title: Keep As Parent Tracker
options.body: Leave the umbrella open as the durable parent while narrower issues and PRs land, accepting that it will remain non-actionable for automation.

options.title: Close As Stale After Repro Request
options.body: Close the umbrella unless the reporter provides a current-main reproduction, but risk losing the cross-surface install/auth/session reliability signal already supported by source and sibling issues.

recommendation.title: Split Into Canonicals
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open only long enough to create or confirm focused canonical issues for each remaining auth, installer, runtime, and session-state surface, then close the umbrella once every acceptance criterion is owned.

likelyOwner.reason: He appears across the current broad code snapshot and adjacent dashboard/auth/session-state surfaces, making him the best available routing owner for the split-or-parent decision.
